newsitem.title: USA: Calif. investor program seen boosting bond orders.
newsitem.headline: Calif. investor program seen boosting bond orders.

text.p: California state treasuer Matt Fong's investor relations program has boosted orders for state bonds and should lower its borrowing costs over time, a state treasury official said Thursday.
L. Steve Spears, deputy state treasurer, told a Bond Buyer California municipal finance conference here that the investor program is having a psoitive impact on state borrowing.
"I do have evidence that visits to investors have resulted in more orders," he said.
Spears said it was unclear whether the program had already lowered state borrowing costs, but added he expected the program to lower future borrowing costs.
As part of the program, Fong and other top state finance officials meet regularly with Wall Street firms and major institutional investors.
The state has $20 billion of long-term bonds outstanding and $3 billion of short-term notes outstanding, Spears said.
